title: Force and torque conditions for equilibrium practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All seven questions use new settings, wording, values and figure geometry. The mapped complete P2 questions ground the distinction between speed and equilibrium, force-diagram reasoning, the two equilibrium conditions, and reaction-force calculation. No official question, number set or diagram is reproduced.

question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: previous-lesson principle retrieval, recognition of both conditions, diagnosis of a motion snapshot, diagnosis of a pure turning effect, one-axis force balance, a resolved-force rigid-body calculation, then a complete two-support equilibrium proof

questions.prompt: State the principle of moments from the previous lesson. Your statement must identify the condition on the body and compare clockwise with anticlockwise moments about the same point.
Which pair of conditions is sufficient for a rigid body to be in equilibrium?

options.A: resultant force is zero and resultant torque is zero
options.B: speed is zero and resultant force is zero
options.C: speed is constant and resultant torque is non-zero
options.D: clockwise moment is zero and vertical force is zero

questions.prompt: A ball is instantaneously at rest at the highest point of a vertical throw. Air resistance is negligible. Which statement is correct?

options.A: It is in equilibrium because its speed is zero.
options.B: It is in equilibrium because its resultant torque is zero.
options.C: It is not in equilibrium because its weight gives a non-zero resultant force.
options.D: It is not in equilibrium because its weight gives a non-zero horizontal force.

questions.prompt: A light horizontal bar has an upward force of 6.0 N at its left end and a downward force of 6.0 N at its right end. No other forces act. What does the bar do?

options.A: It is in equilibrium because the resultant force is zero.
options.B: It has no linear acceleration but has angular acceleration.
options.C: It has linear acceleration but no angular acceleration.
options.D: It has neither linear nor angular acceleration because the forces are equal.

questions.prompt: A lift moves upward at constant velocity. Its total weight is 7200 N. The cable tension is upward and a resistive force of 360 N acts downward. All three forces act along the same vertical line through the lift's centre.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why the moving lift is in equilibrium. Refer to both the force and torque conditions.

questions.prompt: A light horizontal arm AB of length 0.90 m is hinged to a wall at A. A 72 N lamp hangs 0.60 m from A. A cable attached at B pulls upward and toward the wall with tension 80 N at an angle theta above the horizontal. The arm is in equilibrium and sin theta = 0.60 and cos theta = 0.80.

figure.purpose: Provide the spatial geometry and force directions for independent moment and component-force checks
figure.brief: Create an original black-and-white rectangular line diagram. Show wall hinge A, horizontal light arm AB of length 0.90 m, a 72 N downward lamp force 0.60 m from A, and an 80 N cable at B directed upward toward the wall at angle theta above the horizontal. Include sin theta = 0.60 and cos theta = 0.80 as data. Do not show resolved components, reaction directions, equations or answers.
figure.alt_text: A hinged horizontal arm supports a lamp and is held by an angled cable at its free end.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the horizontal and vertical components of the cable tension.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use moments about A to check whether the stated forces can keep the arm in rotational equilibrium.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Determine the horizontal and vertical components of the force exerted on the arm by the hinge. State the direction of each component.

questions.prompt: A 4.0 m uniform footbridge of weight 600 N is supported vertically at ends A and B. A student of weight 480 N stands 1.0 m from A. An equipment case of weight 240 N stands 0.50 m from B. The bridge is stationary and horizontal.

figure.purpose: Support a complete moments-then-forces calculation with distances that must be interpreted from both ends
figure.brief: Create an original black-and-white rectangular line diagram of a 4.0 m uniform footbridge with upward supports at A and B. Show the 600 N bridge weight at the midpoint, a 480 N downward force 1.0 m from A, and a 240 N downward force 0.50 m from B. Label unknown support forces R_A and R_B upward. Do not include equations or numerical answers for the reactions.
figure.alt_text: A four metre bridge has two upward support reactions and three downward weights at labelled positions.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use the principle of moments about A to calculate the support force at B.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use the force condition for equilibrium to calculate the support force at A.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Use moments about B as an independent check of both support forces. Show the two moment totals.
